Sr Supplier Quality Engineer I

Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact

As Axon’s Senior Supplier Quality Engineer I, you will be responsible for providing Quality Engineering support for all Axon products including Conducted Electrical Weapons (CEW), Cartridges, Body Worn Cameras and accessories. You will be responsible for working with suppliers in cooperation with Axon Design Engineering, Quality and Supply Chain. Other significant impacts will come from collaborating on the selection of qualified suppliers, leading the efforts to quantify and improve supplier performance, and providing a positive impact on the quality of new and existing products through a global footprint.

What You’ll Do

Location: Remote in Vietnam (open for candidates from Hanoi/ Bac Ninh/ Hai Phong/ HCM) at our APAC supplier factories with travel up to 80%

Reports to: Supplier Quality Manager

  • New supplier assessment and supplier audit. Engage in selection and evaluation activities of new potential suppliers and conduct onsite auditing of the supplier to assess quality and/or process related requirements. Audit supplier critical manufacturing & inspection processes, policies and procedures to ensure performance and quality standards conform to established Axon Quality requirements.
  • Ensure New Product Introduction (NPI) takes place in accordance with criteria and inspection plans set up and managed by Axon Program Management, Design and Quality. Reviewing product validation with supplier NPI yield, Jira ticket, OQC, FAIR/PPAP, DFM/DFx, PFMEA and Quality control plan (QCP).
  • Working in close collaboration with our supplier partners, facilitate the development and maintenance of PFMEA to quantify supplier process risks and designing processes to prevent the production of defects. Effect robust assembly operations and manufacturing processes through manufacturability assessment and error-proofing methods to prevent operator errors.
  • Assess supplier inspection capabilities onsite as needed (IQC/OQC/IPQC); Assist in generating appropriate inspection plans and evaluate any inspection and process capability studies provided by suppliers (Cpk, Ppk, Gage R&R).
  • Set up the quality goals and quality improvement projects, monitor the yield rate in suppliers and drive supplier to produce high quality parts consistently with yield improvement month to month.
  • Continuously monitor supplier quality performance and facilitate periodic quality/business reviews to drive continual improvements in DPPM, NCMR’s and SCAR’s. Develop, implement, and monitor supplier quality improvement initiatives, including supplier performance management forums, supplier certification, process improvements, cost reduction, and continuing assessment and process audits of suppliers.
  • Through Quality Control Planning, ensure Critical to Quality (CTQ) product characteristics and key process parameters within the supplier’s manufacturing processes are monitored for process capability and capable of repeatedly producing parts to specifications.

What You Bring

  • Minimum 10 years experiences in problem solving related to manufacturing of mechanical parts (i.e. cast metal parts, molded rubber or plastic parts, cast ceramic parts, machined and stamped parts),
  • Very experienced on the NPI process and milestones, the role of SQE for NPI and the key activities in the NPI stages.
  • Good knowledge of quality management system (QMS) requirements, (ISO9001, ESD20.20, IATF16949, IPC-1602, IPC-A-610 or a comparable certificate and quality criteria), minimum five (5) years' experience in audits utilizing ISO9001, IATF16949, VDA 6.3 or a comparable quality management system.
  • Excellent data analysis, root cause analysis, problem resolution and decision-making skills required with thorough working knowledge of QC tools, methods and practices (PPAP, SPC, DOE, PFMEA, Control Plans, GR&R, Lean Manufacturing concepts, DMAIC, 8D Methodology, etc.)
  • Excellent skills of teamwork and collaboration, able to communicate with all levels of the organization and build relationship with suppliers, ability to influence amongst suppliers and internal groups.
  • Ability to operate in a highly dynamic environment to juggle multiple priorities, to react quickly to emergencies. Excellent time management skills and ability to multi-task and methodically manage project milestones.
  • Excellent written and oral communication in English
  • Experience working with statistical software (i.e. QI Macros, Minitab, JMP)
  • Willing to travel frequently (domestic and international)

Preferred education, certification

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering or Material Engineering
  • Green/black belt, CMQ/OE, CQE and CSSBB certifications preferred

Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.

Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they check every box in the job description. If you’re excited about this role and our mission to Protect Life but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification listed here, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Important Notes

The above job description is not intended as, nor should it be construed as, exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, skills, efforts, or working conditions associated with this job. The job description may change or be supplemented at any time in accordance with business needs and conditions.

jobs.description:
IT Operations Analyst

Who are we?

At UpGuard, we are replacing manual security bottlenecks with AI-driven precision. Fresh off a US$75M Series C, we are scaling our infrastructure to process 100 billion risk signals daily. This isn’t just growth; it’s a total reimagining of how the world manages cyber risk.

We build the Cyber Risk Posture Management (CRPM) platform that security teams actually love. By integrating security ratings, threat intel, and agentic AI, we empower organisations to stay ahead of an ever evolving attack surface.

We aren’t just building another tool; we’re defining a category. We provide the autonomy to ship world-class technology and the resources to do it at a global scale.

Where does this role fit in?

  • Build, operate and continually improve the technology platform that lets every UpGuardian work securely, efficiently and with minimal friction.

  • You’ll own the lifecycle of our corporate technology end to end: identity, endpoints, SaaS and the service practices that hold them together. You’ll automate the repetitive parts, instrument the rest, and make security a property of how systems are built rather than a task someone remembers to do.

  • This is an engineering role, not a ticket queue. If you see the same request three times and your first thought is “why is a human still doing this?” - you’ll fit.

  • Security is an outcome of excellent operational engineering here, not the primary function of the role.

What will you do?

Platform, identity and fleet

  • Google Workspace, Okta (or equivalent IdP), and MDM (Kandji, Jamf or similar) across a mostly macOS and ChromeOS fleet

  • You’ll own SaaS administration and lifecycle, asset management, endpoint standards and compliance, and the joiner–mover–leaver process end to end

Zero Trust and secure access

  • Operate and continually improve our Cloudflare Zero Trust environment across ZTNA, Secure Web Gateway, DNS filtering, tunnels and identity and device aware access policies

  • You’ll help move us away from traditional network trust, maintain secure access to internal applications and services, troubleshoot access and connectivity issues, and make sure security controls don’t create unnecessary friction for employees

Automation and internal tooling

  • Automation is the default approach, not a stretch goal. If a task happens more than twice, it’s a candidate for code

  • You’ll work with REST APIs, Python, Apps Script, Terraform, n8n and AI assisted workflows to build internal tooling that removes work rather than making it faster to do by hand

Service operations

  • Incident, problem and change management. Service catalogue, knowledge base, service metrics, capacity planning and operational readiness

  • You’ll define these practices where they don’t exist yet and improve the ones that do

Reliability and continuous improvement

  • Zero touch provisioning, endpoint compliance, fleet health, monitoring, reporting, SaaS governance and self service. Making internal platforms boringly reliable is the goal

Security, embedded

  • Deploy and maintain security controls, harden endpoints, support security incidents, reduce operational risk and keep baselines current

  • Security is part of how you’ll operate the platform rather than a separate function you’ll own

What will you bring?

You won’t have all of this. Tell us which parts you’d be learning, and we’ll tell you honestly whether that works

  • Depth across enterprise SaaS and identity - you’ve administered Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, an IdP such as Okta or Entra, and MDM at organisational scale. You’re comfortable with SSO, SAML, SCIM, DNS and certificates

  • Zero Trust, hands on - you’ve worked with ZTNA, Secure Web Gateway or modern network access controls, ideally Cloudflare Zero Trust or a similar platform such as Zscaler, Netskope, Tailscale or Entra Private Access. You understand identity and device aware access and the principles behind replacing traditional network trust

  • You don’t need to be a Zero Trust specialist, but you should be comfortable taking ownership of an existing Cloudflare implementation, troubleshooting it and making it better

  • You genuinely automate - you write code using Python, Apps Script or similar, work confidently with REST APIs, and can point to internal tooling you’ve shipped that removed recurring work permanently

  • Fleet management maturity - you’ve worked with macOS at scale, zero touch provisioning and endpoint compliance baselines

  • Service operations experience - you’ve run incident and change practices, defined metrics and built documentation people actually use

  • Security and infrastructure fundamentals - you’re comfortable with endpoint hardening, identity security, DNS, certificates, secure network access and making sensible risk trade offs

  • Process improvement instinct - you make the system better, not just the outcome of one request

What will give you an edge?

  • Terraform or other Infrastructure as Code

  • Cloudflare

  • n8n or similar orchestration

  • AI and LLM-assisted workflows

  • Deep macOS expertise

  • Chrome Enterprise

  • Working in a security-first or audited environment (SOC 2, ISO 27001)

What's in it for you?

  • Monthly Lifestyle subsidy: Use this for financial, physical, and mental well-being

  • WFH set-up allowance: To ensure you have the right environment to work in, we will help you get set up within your first 3 months at UpGuard

  • $1500 USD annual Learning & Development allowance: To support your career development, all team members will be able to expense development opportunities against this allowance

  • Annual leave: PTO plus two additional UpGuardian leave days to give you time to recharge your batteries.

  • 18 weeks paid Parental Leave: Irrespective of parenting role

  • Personal Leave Allowance: This includes sick & carer’s leave

  • Fully remote working environment: While we have physical offices in Sydney & Hobart, we do not mandate compulsory attendance

  • Top-spec hardware: All team members will be provided with top-spec laptops for their role

  • Generative AI subsidy: UpGuard provides paid subscriptions for all team members to access generative AI tools to support their work

  • Health Insurance: Access to comprehensive coverage.

UpGuard is a Certified Great Place to Work® in the US, Australia, UK and India, establishing its position as a leading global technology employer. 99% of team members agree that UpGuard is a great place to work! Apply now to find out why!

As an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer, qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status.

For applications to positions in the United States, please note, at this time, we can only support hiring in the following US states: CA, MD, MA, IL, OR, WA, CO, TX, FL, PA, LA, MO, or DC.

Before starting work with us, you will need to undertake a national police history check and reference checks. Also, please note that at this time, we cannot support candidates requiring visa sponsorship or relocation.

jobs.title: 3D & Motion Designer | Robotics
jobs.description:
3D & Motion Designer | Robotics

Your tasks

  • Get CAD ready for rendering: Turn heavy mechanical assemblies from engineering into clean 3D assets that render, animate and run in real time without falling apart. The hardware stands in our workshop, and the next machine is never far behind.
  • Show what is inside: Exploded views, cutaways and assembly animations that explain the mechanics without a technical drawing, so customers understand the tech behind the product.
  • Materials that look real: Build shaders for aluminum, stainless steel, glass, rubber, carbon, plastics, displays and LEDs, so a render reads as the actual object rather than as a render. Scenes, materials and rigs stay organized, so the next project does not start from zero.
  • Motion design in a house style: Titles, typography, transitions, logo animation, and 2D animation for interface elements like animated displays and icons. It should look like us, not like a template pack.
  • Editing and post: Footage from the workshop and tests, mixed with 3D work, becomes what we use on the website, on social, at trade shows and in investor meetings. Editing, grading, sound, subtitles, and a version that fits each channel.
  • Put AI to work: You use AI and generative tools (e.g. comfy) where they actually save time, whether that is concepting, cleanup or upscaling. You keep testing what is new, keep what earns a place in the pipeline, and drop the rest.

Your profile

  • Background: A degree in motion design, animation or media design, or a self taught route with a reel that makes the question pointless.
  • Experience: At least two years of hands on work, whether from an internship, freelance jobs, a studio or your own projects. What the work looks like matters more to us than where it was made.
  • CAD is not new to you: You have opened engineering data before and know roughly what happens when a heavy assembly meets a render engine.
  • Reel: Hard surfaces, metal, glass and light. Even one personal project done properly tells us more than ten client jobs you only assisted on.
  • Tools: Experience in Blender and Cinema 4D, Octane is a plus. After Effects and either Premiere for the cut.
  • How you work: Hands on and fast to a first version. You get things finished instead of perfect, and you notice when a detail stops being worth the hours.
  • Languages: Fluent English. Good German is a real plus.

Why us?

  • Your work is what people see of us: Almost everything the outside world sees of our robots comes out of your hands, and you decide how that looks.
  • Everything under one roof: Labs, workshop and test rigs are in the same Kreuzberg building. The engineer you need is a walk away, not a ticket.
  • Room to get better: Paid learning time and a personal budget for it, projects where something is allowed to not work the first time, and support for portfolio work and conference talks as the company becomes known.
  • Benefits: A benefits package you put together yourself, covering mobility, home setup, health or food. Plus one extra paid day off a year for volunteering or a project you care about.

Send us a link to your work. Best case it includes something you took from CAD data to a finished render, with a note on how. Skip the cover letter.

Process: Intro call -> Portfolio deep-dive -> Half-day on-site visit with a small design exercise -> Offer.

We build robots for everyone, so we want a team that reflects that. We hire on what you can do, and we welcome applications from people who are underrepresented in 3D and motion. If you don't tick every box but think this is your job, apply anyway.

jobs.description:
Senior Technical Support Analyst

About us

At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels. 

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 

We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel.

Introducing the Workplace Technology team at Trainline 👋

Our Workplace Technology team owns and manages the corporate technology stack of business and workplace solutions, driving innovative, cost efficient, future ways of working.

The Tech Support team is a critical part of the Workplace Technology team, ensuring Tier 2 and Tier 3 support services are delivered effectively and efficiently within a culture of continual service improvement, aligned to Trainline values.

The team is principally responsible for end user computing across a MacOS estate under central management using JAMF Pro, and a Microsoft Windows estate integrated with Azure Active Directory and Microsoft Windows Servers. This is a highly visible team, also providing dedicated AV/VC support for meeting rooms and internal events — ensuring high availability, instilling trust, and enabling a seamless experience for Executive-level presenters.

About the Role

This is not just a senior technical position — it is a leadership role within the team. We are looking for someone who takes genuine ownership: of problems, of standards, of team capability, and of the overall service we deliver to Trainliners. You will be the go-to person when things get complex, the one who sets the bar for quality, and the one who actively lifts others to reach it.

You will work closely with the Workplace Technology Lead, acting as a technical anchor for the team — driving consistency, mentoring your peers, championing best practices, and making sure nothing important falls through the cracks. If you see something that isn't right, you fix it. If a junior engineer is stuck, you help them through it. If a process is broken, you own improving it.

As a Senior IT Support Analyst, you'll be responsible for... 🚝

Technical Leadership & Team Ownership

• Acting as the technical escalation point for the team — owning complex incidents end-to-end and ensuring nothing stalls without clear direction

• Mentoring and upskilling junior and mid-level engineers: pairing on problems, reviewing their work, and sharing knowledge deliberately and consistently

Incident, Problem & Request Management

• Owning the full incident lifecycle for complex and high-priority issues — from triage and investigation through to resolution and post-incident review

• Conducting deep root cause analysis: reviewing logs, correlating cross-system patterns, engaging third-party vendors, and documenting findings clearly

• Ensuring the team's ticket queue is healthy — proactively monitoring dashboards, reassigning where needed, and preventing SLA breaches before they happen

• Driving problem management: identifying recurring incidents, initiating investigations, and leading permanent fix efforts rather than accepting repeat workarounds

• Owning escalation quality — ensuring issues are fully investigated, clearly documented, and appropriately packaged before being escalated to Tier 3 or vendors

Microsoft 365, Azure AD & Identity Management

• Advanced administration of Microsoft 365 services: Exchange Online, SharePoint, Teams, OneDrive, and the M365 Security & Compliance Centre

• Azure Active Directory: user and group lifecycle, Conditional Access policy design and troubleshooting, SSPR, MFA enforcement, and RBAC

• Leading SSO/SAML integrations for new SaaS platforms — configuring, testing, and documenting alongside the security team

• Owning access package governance and token management processes, ensuring alignment with policy and audit requirements

• Supporting licence governance: E3/E5 procurement, assignment, cost awareness, and flagging any out-of-policy requests to the appropriate stakeholder

AV/VC & Events Support

• Taking ownership of the AV/VC estate — maintaining full health of meeting room systems including display hardware, conferencing codecs, room controllers, and peripherals

• Proactive health monitoring using remote administration tools, with performance analytics and regular firmware/software updates

• Leading in-person and remote technical delivery for internal events and Executive/all-hands presentations

• Acting as the senior point of contact for AV issues, ensuring fast resolution and minimal meeting disruption across all sites

• Documenting AV configurations and building runbooks that enable the wider team to support the estate confidently

End User Computing & Device Management

• Advanced MacOS and Windows 11 management via JAMF Pro and Microsoft Intune/Autopilot — including policy authoring, troubleshooting complex deployment failures, and estate-wide configuration management

• Overseeing the quality of on/off-boarding processes: laptop builds, IT inductions, IAM compliance, deprovisioning, and asset retrieval

• Driving IT Asset Management maturity: inventory accuracy, lifecycle planning, hardware refresh adherence, and secure disposal compliance

• Working knowledge of Android and Linux environments; able to support edge cases confidently

Security, Compliance & Governance

• Championing security standards across the team — ensuring all activity aligns with ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, and internal policy

• Leading the team's contribution to audit and compliance reviews: ensuring evidence is well-organised, processes are followed, and findings are acted on

• Owning the leavers process for sensitive cases — coordinating deprovisioning, data access controls, and asset recovery in line with CISO and privacy requirements

• Supporting MFA rollout, access policy governance, and SSO governance initiatives with appropriate rigour and documentation

• Ensuring all advice given to the team is backed by security sign-off and documented reference — not informal Slack approvals

Documentation, Process & Continuous Improvement

• Owning and continuously improving the team's knowledge base — SOPs, runbooks, known error records, and onboarding guides must be accurate, accessible, and up to date

• Identifying process inefficiencies and owning their improvement: not just flagging them but designing, implementing, and embedding the fix

• Driving automation and tooling improvements — proposing and where possible implementing AI, ML, and scripting solutions that reduce toil and improve consistency

• Ensuring approvals, decisions, and audit trails live in the ticketing system — not in Slack channels

Our Tech Stack requires solid experience of 🔑

• Windows 11 and Apple ecosystem in an enterprise environment (+ working knowledge of Android & Linux)

• Mobile Device Management: JAMF Pro and Microsoft Intune — policy creation, complex troubleshooting, and deployment strategy

• Microsoft 365 administration — Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, and M365 Security & Compliance Centre

• Azure Active Directory — user lifecycle, Conditional Access, SSPR, MFA, and RBAC at an administrative level

• Modern workplace solutions: Autopilot, Intune, MFA, and cloud migration strategies

• Platform integrations, SSO/SAML — configuration, fault diagnosis, and documentation

• AV/VC hardware and software: room systems, conferencing platforms, and peripheral management

• Networks: TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, LAN, WAN, and wireless

• Windows Command Line / PowerShell & Apple Scripting / BASH — beyond basics; able to write and adapt scripts

• SaaS applications including Slack, Atlassian suite, and cloud printing solutions

Desirable Certifications:

We'd love to hear from you if you... 🔍

• Have a genuine security-first mindset and understand why governance and audit trails matter

• Spot broken processes and own fixing them — not just flagging them

• Work autonomously under pressure, exercising sound judgement and knowing when to escalate

• Are happy to be onsite as needed, including for events and critical incidents

If you're a senior engineer who wants to do more than close tickets — who wants to shape a team, own a service, and leave things better than you found them — this is the role for you.

The Interview Process 🚉

The modern studio is located in the vibrant technology hub of Cambridge (UK). You’ll also share responsibility for the performance, reliability, and cost‑efficiency of our online services, working with other discipline leads to ensure we deliver smooth, scalable, and engaging experiences for our players.

Chief of Staff to the CTO - Engineering

Are you looking to have an impact on the daily life of millions of entrepreneurs in France (and tomorrow in Europe)?

Are you looking for a work environment that values trust, proactivity, and autonomy?

Then Pennylane is the right place for you !

 

Our vision

We aim to become the most beloved financial Operating System of French SMEs and Accounting Firms (and soon, European ones).

We help entrepreneurs rid themselves of time-consuming tasks related to accounting and finance while providing them with access to key financial information to assist in making the best decisions for their business.

 

About us

Pennylane is one of the fastest growing Fintechs in France (and soon to be in Europe!)

 

In 5 years of existence, we’ve managed to :

💻 Make ourselves known as a groundbreaking accounting and financial software for small businesses and their accountants

💰 Raise a total of €400 millions, including from Sequoia, the famous fund from the Silicon Valley who invested early in companies like Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal and much more...

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Grow from 7 cofounders to 1000 happy Pennylaners : we’re now recognized as one of the greatest places to work in France (and also remotely), with a 4.6/5 rating on Glassdoor.

🌍 Build an international environment with more than 25 nationalities, with a strong remote-friendly culture, where 30% of the employees are already working from all parts of Europe

🤝 Earn the trust of thousands of customers and accounting firms and obtain outstanding ratings

🚀 Already more than 900,000 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and over 6000 accounting firms use Pennylane in France!

 

In 2024, we implemented an organizational structure built around business 'tracks'. This approach integrates key stakeholders across marketing, sales, product, and customer care into unified teams focused on specific product lines or client segments. Each track operates as a mini-business, empowered with dedicated resources (e.g., product marketing, data analytics, and operational support) and direct accountability for performance.

 
 

Why this role matters at Pennylane

 

As Chief of Staff to the CTO, you operate as a senior leader in the Tech organisation. Your leverage does not come from managing teams but from owning the hardest problems that sit between them, and from being technical enough to earn the trust of the other engineering leaders.

You are the person the CTO trusts with ambiguous, org-wide problems. You turn that ambiguity into a clear framing, a decision, an owner and a measurable outcome.

This is not a coordination role. You are expected to have opinions on engineering strategy, staffing choices and technical trade-offs, and to defend them in front of the Tech leadership team.

 

Team and Context

Pennylane's Tech organisation is 70+ squads, each led by an Engineering Manager working with a PM and a Product Designer. We serve 1.5m+ customers and we want to scale in Europe. At that size, the hard problems are no longer inside a squad: how the organisation plans, how it decides, how it measures itself, how it invests in foundations without stalling product delivery. That is your perimeter.

You report directly to Quentin, Co-founder & CTO. Your influence comes from the scope of what you own and from credibility with senior engineering leaders, which is why we ask for a technical background. As the organisation grows, this role can evolve towards a management position.

Key missions

Engineering strategy and transversal initiatives

  • Own the strategic, cross-organization initiatives that no single squad can carry: platform or architecture programmes, reliability and quality step-changes, engineering productivity, technical debt paydown

  • Frame the problem, build the technical and business case, secure alignment across Engineering, Product and Security to drive execution

  • Lead the Tech side of company-level programmes (e.g. European expansion, major compliance or infrastructure shifts) alongside the rest of the Tech leadership

Planning & Performance tracking

  • Own the Tech planning cycle: collect the inputs, surface the trade-offs (capacity vs. platform, run vs. new bets), and drive the arbitration with Tech leadership

  • Drive the definition and calibration of Tech OKRs, and hold the organisation accountable

  • Define what "good" looks like for a 70+ squad engineering organization and build the metrics that measure it (delivery cadence, reliability, quality, staffing and attrition, engineering satisfaction)

Decision-making and leadership cadence

  • Own the Tech leadership operating system: staff meetings, QBRs, roadmap and architecture reviews. You design them, set the agenda, write or commission the pre-reads, frame the decisions to be made, and make sure decisions land

  • Maintain the CTO's decision log: what was decided, by whom, with what trade-off, and what happened next

  • Raise the quality of decision-making across the Tech leadership team

Communication

jobs.title: Junior Computational Geometry Engineer
jobs.description:
Junior Computational Geometry Engineer
SAEKI - Manufacturing at software speed

Europe's defense industrial base cannot respond at the speed modern conflict requires. Legacy suppliers operate on month-long timelines. Tribal knowledge is retiring. Supply chains are fragile. SAEKI is building the operating system for autonomous factories - the infrastructure that lets Europe manufacture mission-critical components at software speed.


The Role

As a Junior Computational Geometry Engineer, you work on the geometry core of our Manufacturing Intelligence stack: the engine that takes an arbitrary customer CAD model, reasons about how to build it, and then proves that we built it right.
You start on well-scoped parts of that engine, next to the engineers who built it, and grow into owning them. Your code runs in the factory.


What We're Looking For

  • Foundations. Degree in computer science, mathematics, mechanical engineering or a related field, with real depth in geometry, linear algebra and numerics. Internships, thesis work or serious side projects count. We do not expect years of production experience.
  • B-rep Basics. You are comfortable with topology, NURBS, meshes and point clouds. You may never have shipped a robust boolean, and you still understand why floating-point robustness destroys naive implementations, and you want to learn how the field handles it.
  • Kernel Exposure. You have worked with a geometry kernel and mesh libraries in at least one project: OpenCASCADE, CGAL, libigl, Open3D, PCL, Parasolid or comparable.
  • Technical Ability. Solid modern C++ (17+) plus Python for tooling and rapid iteration. Rust is welcome. You write code others can read, test and maintain.
  • Manufacturing Curiosity. You want to understand what happens once geometry meets a spindle, a nozzle or a fixture. CNC, additive or metrology exposure is a bonus, never a requirement.
  • First Principles Thinker. You reason by physics and mathematics, not analogy. When an algorithm fails on a real part, you dig until you know whether the bug sits in the code, the model or the assumption.
  • Learning Speed. You take direct feedback, apply it immediately, and close your own knowledge gaps without waiting to be taught.
  • Industrial Grit. You want to stand next to the machine in Germany and watch your output run. The feedback loop between your code and cutting metal is the point.
  • On-site. Ability to work in person at our HQ in Zurich, Switzerland.


What we're not looking for

  • Researchers who want to publish and hand off. You ship.
  • CAD users. This is a role for people who build the tools, not drive them.
  • Engineers who need a clean spec. The problem is defined by the part, the machine, and the customer - you'll help define it.
  • People who treat “it works on the test model” as done. Real customer CAD is broken, degenerate, and adversarial. That is the job.
  • Engineers who are uncomfortable with ambiguity or rapidly changing priorities.


What we offer

  • Mission: Rebuild the industrial sovereignty of the West. Your work directly enables production of mission-critical hardware for defense and space.
  • Total Ownership: High-stakes autonomy in your domain. You own both the problems and the solutions - and have the authority to execute.
  • The Environment: Access to a 8,000 m² state-of-the-art facility featuring 5-axis CNCs, industrial robots, and industrial 3D printers. Your algorithms run on real hardware from day one.
  • The Team: "Special Forces" model. Everyone senior, everyone ships. No politics, no bureaucracy. Direct feedback, high standards.
  • Compensation: Competitive salary + meaningful equity.
  • Location: Zurich HQ, with occasional time at Factory ONE in Munich.



Apply

  • Resume: Focus on the geometry work you have actually done. Thesis, internships, projects, coursework.
  • GitHub/Portfolio: Show us the hardest problem you have solved. Code, a write-up, or a part that came off a machine because of you.
  • Coverletter: Why this mission? Why now? What would you build first?

jobs.title: Maître de conférences en Cybersécurité
jobs.description:
Maître de conférences en Cybersécurité

IMT Atlantique, reconnue internationalement pour la qualité de sa recherche, est une école d’ingénieurs de premier plan sous la tutelle du ministère de l'industrie et du numérique, classée dans les trois principaux classements internationaux (THE, SHANGHAI, QS).

 

Le poste est ouvert sur le campus de Rennes au sein du département SRCD (Systèmes Réseaux, Cybersécurité et Droit du numérique). Le département SRCD est composé de 24 enseignant.e.s-chercheurs.euses permanent.e.s, plus de 10 post-doctorant.e.s et ingénieur.e.s contractuel.le.s, et 30 doctorant.e.s. Ses domaines d'activité recouvrent tous les aspects de l'enseignement et de la recherche en systèmes et réseaux au sens large, en cybersécurité, et en droit et économie des activités numériques. Dans le cadre de ses activités de recherche, la personne recrutée rejoindra l’équipe SOTERN (Self Protecting the Future Internet) du département D2 du laboratoire IRISA (UMR CNRS 6074), l'un des plus grands laboratoires de recherche français (+ de 850 personnes) dans le domaine de l'informatique et des nouvelles technologies de l'information.

Enjeux et profil attendu sur le thématique de recherche

 

Deux enjeux majeurs présentent actuellement un impact conséquent sur la recherche et l’innovation en Cybersécurité. D’un côté, l’intelligence artificielle par ses développements récents et les attendus pour les années à venir décuple les possibilités offertes aux attaquants pour mettre en œuvre de nouvelles attaques, tout autant qu’aux structures défensives (type SOC par exemple) pour détecter, corréler et contrer des incidents de sécurité. D’un autre côté, les cibles des attaques évoluent et les architectures déployées dans les réseaux opérationnels (systèmes industriels, réseaux intra-véhiculaires, avionique, opérateurs d’importance vitale) nécessitent de nouveaux moyens de détection et protection face à une menace grandissante.

Le profil recherché pour ce poste s’inscrit ainsi dans la thématique de la sécurité des réseaux au sens large. Il sera plus spécifiquement recherché soit une expertise relative aux architectures, protocoles et algorithmes d’intelligence artificielle pour la sécurité des réseaux ou de l’IA (apprentissage fédéré, sécurité des architectures d’IA type Model Context Protocol (MCP), etc.), soit une expertise sur la sécurité des réseaux opérationnels (OT) quel qu’en soit le cadre applicatif.  

 

Enjeux et profil attendu en enseignement

 

Positionnée sur 3 campus attractifs, IMT Atlantique affiche une forte dynamique internationale tout en restant à taille humaine. Dans ces différents cursus BAC+5 (formations d’ingénieurs et de masters-DNM), les étudiants sont confrontés, via des approches pédagogiques variées, à des situations-problèmes concrets. L’école a ainsi pour ambition de former de jeunes professionnels à fort potentiel, capables de mobiliser un large spectre de compétences en situation réelle, dans des environnements (production, recherche, création d’activité, etc.) et des domaines socio-économiques variés.

 

Impliqué tant en tronc commun que dans les parcours électifs, la personne recrutée contribuera aussi bien dans sa spécialité Cybersécurité que dans des activités transverses, interdisciplinaires ou en lien avec des entreprises : tutorat de projets / stages, soutenances, accompagnement, etc. La personne recrutée sera encouragée à contribuer, dans un esprit de collaboration, à l’évolution cohérente des programmes d’études, en proposant de nouveaux projets, programmes et méthodologies pédagogiques, particulièrement inspirés et soutenus par les exigences et les partenariats industriels. https://www.imt-atlantique.fr/fr/formation

 

En cohérence avec le profil de la personne candidate, il sera demandé de prendre en main les thématiques d’enseignement parmi les suivantes : IA et Cybersécurité (IA offensive, IA pour la protection des infrastructures, sécurité de l’IA), Sécurité des systèmes industriels, participation puis prise de responsabilité de l’organisation du CTF Hack’lantique, et plus largement une participation aux différents enseignements en Cybersécurité.

 

Responsabilité collective et implication dans le développement économique

En effet une attention particulière sera portée sur la capacité du candidat à s’impliquer dans la vie collective de l’école : contribuer, ou piloter des projets transverses (par exemple sur la transition écologique, prendre des responsabilités (programmes de formation, projets de recherche, équipes pédagogiques ou de recherche) ou participer à des instances : comité de l’enseignement, conseil d’école, comité social d’administration.

En outre dans un environnement de relations privilégiées avec de grands partenaires industriels nationaux et internationaux, ainsi qu’un réseau dense de PME, Start up, l’enseignant chercheur recruté contribuera au rayonnement de l’école et au développement économique, notamment au travers de la valorisation de ses travaux par le dépôt de brevet ou le transfert de technologies. Avec 257 enseignants-chercheurs permanents, 2450 étudiants dont 399 doctorants, IMT Atlantique produit chaque année 655 publications et lève 28.3M€ de fonds de recherche.

jobs.description:
Professeur(e) en Data/IA appliquée aux Matériaux et Procédés Rattaché(e) au Centre Institut Clément Ader Albi (ICA-A)

ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE :

École du ministère en charge de l’industrie, IMT Mines Albi est une école de l’Institut Mines-Télécom (IMT), 1er groupe d’écoles d’ingénieurs et de management de France. À l’avant-garde des enjeux industriels et académiques sur la scène internationale, elle agit comme un moteur scientifique et économique territorial en combinant ses quatre missions : former des ingénieurs en intégrant la dynamique du développement durable, faire de la recherche scientifique, contribuer au développement économique et diffuser la culture des sciences, des techniques et de l’innovation, en un cercle vertueux et porteur d’innovation.

Son positionnement en matière de formation et de recherche place IMT Mines Albi comme une école de référence sur trois des quatre thématiques de l’IMT : l’industrie du futur responsable ; l’énergie, l’économie circulaire et la société ; l’ingénierie, la santé et le bien-être. IMT Mines Albi s’est dotée en 2023, pour une période quinquennale, d’un plan stratégique décliné en sept grandes actions, répondant aux orientations stratégiques du groupe IMT auquel elle appartient.

 

IMT Mines Albi représente :

  • 985 élèves-ingénieurs et chercheurs en formation ;

  • 300 personnels ;

  • un budget consolidé de 32 M€ ;

  • trois centres de formation et de recherche : Institut Clément Ader Albi (ICA-A), RAPSODEE et Centre Génie Industriel.

 

 

Le Centre Institut Clément Ader Albi (ICA-A) est un centre de formation et de recherche d’IMT Mines Albi. Il rassemble 70 personnes, dont 20 enseignants-chercheurs.

Au titre de la formation, il est un acteur de la formation ingénieur généraliste d’IMT Mines Albi, sous statut étudiant ou apprenti, et porte l’option « Matériaux et procédés avancés pour les transports de demain ».

 

Au titre de la recherche, il est partie intégrante de l’Institut Clément Ader (ICA – UMR CNRS 5312), laboratoire rassemblant 250 personnes et développant des thématiques scientifiques axées sur l’ingénierie et la mécanique des matériaux, notamment dans le domaine de l’aéronautique. Ses cinq établissements de tutelle sont l’INSA de Toulouse, l’ISAE-SUPAERO, l’Université Paul Sabatier, IMT Mines Albi et le CNRS.

 

Site Internet de l’ICA : https://ica.cnrs.fr/

 

L’ICA traite des études sur les structures, les systèmes et les processus mécaniques. Ses secteurs d’activité sont les industries mécaniques, avec un accent particulier sur l’aérospatiale, l’espace, le transport et l’énergie.

Le centre Institut Clément Ader Albi contribue aux quatre groupes de recherche de l’ICA :

  • Matériaux et Structures Composites ;

  • Surfaces, Usinage, Matériaux, Outillages ;

  • Métrologie, Identification, Contrôle, Surveillance ;

  • Modélisation des Systèmes et Microsystèmes Mécaniques.

 

Le champ d’action d’ICA-A est d’optimiser les outillages ou les procédés de mise en forme des matériaux (métaux, composites, polymères, verres, etc.) ainsi que d’étudier les relations entre microstructure, procédé et comportement, en particulier pour les secteurs de l’aéronautique et du spatial. Ses activités sont fortement expérimentales, mais également numériques.

 

ICA-A possède sa propre plateforme de recherche sur le campus d’IMT Mines Albi, la plateforme MIMAUSA. ICA-A est une Zone à Régime Restrictif (ZRR) depuis 2021.

 

DESCRIPTION DU POSTE :

De manière générale, la personne recrutée participera aux projets pédagogiques de l’école, aux missions de formation, aux activités de recherche et de transfert de technologies, au montage et au suivi des activités contractuelles ainsi qu’aux collaborations nationales et internationales. Elle contribuera activement au développement de ces activités et pourra être amenée à exercer des responsabilités administratives et d’encadrement.

 

La personne recrutée aura notamment vocation à assurer :

 

  • des responsabilités pédagogiques : responsable de cycle d’enseignement, responsable d’option, responsable de Master ou Mastère, responsable d’unité d’enseignement ;

  • et/ou des responsabilités en recherche : directeur de centre, directeur de centre adjoint, responsable de groupe de recherche, responsable d’axe de recherche, responsable de plateforme ;

  • et/ou des responsabilités liées au transfert industriel et au développement économique ;

  • et/ou des responsabilités transverses, comme par exemple : responsable de processus ou sous-processus, responsable thématique international.

 

Activités de formation

Dans le programme de formation du centre ICA-A, la personne recrutée participera aux activités pédagogiques et d’enseignement d’IMT Mines Albi.

 Dans ce cadre, elle sera amenée à :

  • contribuer à l’évolution des programmes pédagogiques et assurer des enseignements dans les domaines de l’analyse de données et de l’intelligence artificielle appliquées à l’écoconception, au développement de nouveaux matériaux, à leur mise en forme, ainsi qu’à l’étude de leurs mécanismes de dégradation et à la prévision de la durée de vie des pièces ;

  • accompagner et organiser les missions de formation de l’École sous leurs diverses formes : formation initiale ou continue, sous statut étudiant ou salarié, et formations débouchant sur des diplômes de Mastère ou de Master ;

  • participer au montage ou au pilotage de nouvelles formations (Mastère ou Master), prendre la responsabilité d’une ou plusieurs unités d’enseignement, s’impliquer dans l’organisation et le suivi de projets étudiants, ainsi que dans l’élaboration et l’exploitation de MOOC ;

  • encadrer des projets avec mises en situation, des stages et des travaux de fin d’études.

 

Activités de recherche

 Dans le programme de recherche du centre ICA-A, la personne recrutée :

  • proposera une démarche scientifique pour le développement de méthodes innovantes d’exploitation et d’analyse de données et d’utilisation de l’IA, capables de répondre aux exigences d’un dialogue essais/calcul multi-échelles. Ces méthodes seront utilisées pour le suivi ou la compréhension des propriétés des matériaux en lien avec leur fabrication ou avec le suivi de l’état de santé de pièces en service dans des environnements potentiellement critiques (hautes ou basses températures, contraintes mécaniques fortes, atmosphères oxydantes ou corrosives) ;

  • sera rattachée à un des groupes de recherche du laboratoire ICA (UMR 5312)

  • devra démontrer sa capacité à développer une activité contractuelle avec les entreprises et à participer au montage de chaires d’enseignement et de recherche en relation avec les entreprises ;

  • contribuera au rayonnement scientifique d’IMT Mines Albi et du laboratoire ICA par une implication active dans l’encadrement de thèses et de post-doctorants, par une production scientifique significative, par la diffusion de l’information scientifique lors de conférences et par l’organisation de manifestations scientifiques ;

  • sera amenée à monter des projets collaboratifs en lien avec les autres centres de recherche d’IMT Mines Albi : RAPSODEE et CGI.

 

 

Activités de valorisation et de développement économique

Dans le programme de valorisation et de développement économique du centre ICA-A, la personne recrutée devra :

  • renforcer le développement économique local et régional par l’accompagnement d’entités en incubation ou en prospection d’incubation au sein d’IMT Mines Albi ;

  • et/ou soutenir les initiatives ponctuelles en répondant aux demandes d’accompagnement (thèses CIFRE, contrats directs) formulées par les entreprises, en particulier les TPE et PME, dans son domaine d’expertise ;

  • et/ou accompagner la dynamique industrielle en s’impliquant dans la mise en place et le pilotage de chaires industrielles ou de laboratoires communs permettant d’optimiser le transfert technologique et méthodologique à destination des acteurs locaux, régionaux ou nationaux.

 

Évolution des responsabilités

À moyen terme, la personne recrutée pourra se voir proposer :

  • des responsabilités pédagogiques : responsable de cycle d’enseignement, responsable d’option, responsable de Master ou Mastère, responsable d’unité d’enseignement ;

  • et/ou des responsabilités en recherche : responsable de groupe de recherche, responsable d’axe de recherche, responsable de plateforme ;

  • et/ou des responsabilités liées au transfert industriel et au développement économique.

 

 

PROFIL RECHERCHE :

La personne candidate devra justifier d’une expérience d’au moins huit ans en recherche dans la spécialité Data/IA appliquée aux matériaux et procédés.

 

Une qualification aux fonctions de professeur en 60e section du CNU est fortement souhaitée.

 

En outre, la personne candidate devra :

 

  • présenter une expertise scientifique dans plusieurs des domaines suivants : jumeaux numériques, dynamique des systèmes, machine learning, deep learning, réseaux de neurones, deep optimisation ;

  • justifier d’expériences dans la conception et le pilotage de programmes pédagogiques ;

  • faire preuve d’une forte capacité et d’un goût prononcé pour l’animation d’une équipe de recherche ;

  • posséder de réelles qualités relationnelles, ainsi qu’un sens développé des relations humaines et des valeurs collectives ;

  • présenter une production scientifique cohérente avec les standards nationaux et internationaux et une expérience significative de l’encadrement doctoral.

 

AU-DELÀ DE L’ENVIRONNEMENT PROFESSIONNEL, POURQUOI NOUS REJOINDRE ? 

  • Un cadre de travail agréable sur un campus de 22 hectares ;

  • un forfait cadre avec 49 jours de congés annuels (congés + RTT) ;

  • le télétravail possible ;

  • une restauration administrative sur place ;

  • une aide à la mobilité durable pour les trajets domicile-travail ;

  • une action sociale (protection sociale complémentaire et aide aux familles) ;

  • une aide au déménagement ;

  • une aide à l’intégration sur le territoire : https://www.grand-albigeois.fr/entreprendre/creer-se-developper/soutien-au-recrutement-salarie/

 

INFORMATIONS COMPLÉMENTAIRES :

  • Statut : fonctionnaire ou détachement sur notre cadre de gestion.

  • À usage interne :

• Catégorie du poste et métier de référence : métier A – Professeur, Directeur d’études et Directeur de recherches

• Métier(s) de référence des agents pouvant postuler : toutes catégories

 

  • Localisation : Albi – IMT Mines Albi.

 

  • Date d’ouverture des candidatures : 1er octobre 2026.

  • Date limite de candidature : 1er novembre 2026.

  • Date de prise de fonction souhaitée : 1er janvier 2027.

 

Les postes offerts au recrutement sont ouverts à toutes et tous avec, sur demande, des aménagements pour les candidates et candidats en situation de handicap.

 

Contacts :

Sur le contenu du poste :
Mme Anaïs BARASINSKI – Directrice de Centre
 

Sur les aspects administratifs/RH :
Mme Marie GILLET – Responsable Recrutement et Développement des Compétences
 

Protection des données

Dans le cadre du règlement général sur la protection des données, les candidates et candidats sont informés que les données les concernant seront conservées par l’administration pendant une durée maximale de deux ans, sauf demande contraire de leur part précisée dans la lettre de motivation.

STAGE - Junior Fullstack Engineer
Notre mission ⚖️

Chez Doctrine, nous construisons le leader de l’IA juridique en Europe.

Notre conviction ? Le droit ne doit pas être ralenti par des tâches répétitives. Il doit être augmenté par une IA spécialisée, conçue pour comprendre, analyser et produire du raisonnement juridique avec un haut niveau d’exigence.

Notre ambition ? Permettre aux professionnels du droit de gagner en fiabilité, en efficacité et en sérénité, grâce à une plateforme unique, exhaustive et sécurisée.

Aujourd’hui, 27 000 professionnels du droit, répartis dans cinq pays (France, Italie, Allemagne, Espagne, Luxembourg), nous font confiance.

Notre développement est guidé par une approche claire : une vision globale, ancrée dans une compréhension fine des spécificités locales.

Derrière cette ambition, une équipe d’environ 250 personnes, réunies autour d’un même objectif : accompagner les juristes et avocats à toutes les étapes de leur travail, de l’analyse à la rédaction.

Et nous n’en sommes qu’au début.


Contexte du stage

Depuis des années, Doctrine propose une fonctionnalité d’envoi de décision de justice en France à ses clients. Cela est une source précieuse de décisions de justice qui permet à Doctrine d’enrichir sa base de données (c'est-à-dire son legal graph) avec des décisions qui n’ont pas pu être ajoutées par nos processus habituels.

Le but de ce stage est l’internationalisation de cette fonctionnalité de manière à ce qu’elle soit utilisable dans tous les autres pays où Doctrine est actif (Italie, Allemagne).

Les tâches principales seront :
  • Le développement d’une application minimale pour la revue et validation des décisions de justice mises en ligne par nos utilisateurs pour nos juristes avant leur publication.
  • La migration du processus legacy d’upload français actuel pour se conformer au processus commun (internationalisé).
Une fois que le processus de mise en ligne de décisions par nos utilisateurs sera internationalisé, le ou la stagiaire pourra travailler sur des tâches d’amélioration de l’application de revue de décisions dans le but d’aider notre équipe de juristes à mieux traiter le volume de décisions mises en ligne.

Exemples de pistes d’amélioration (non exhaustif)
  • Application de techniques d’OCR sur les documents pour faciliter leur validation.
  • Détection via LLM d’attributs des décisions (niveau de confidentialité, juridiction, domaine du droit, cour, …) pour faciliter leur validation.
  • Aide au retrait de contenu qui n’est pas le texte de la décision (pages blanches, notification à l’avocat, …).
    Le ou la stagiaire devra participer à la définition de la solution et sa réalisation. Il ou elle rejoindra l’équipe Italie et sera amené·e à travailler avec les équipes des autres pays (principalement l’équipe France) et l’équipe légale. Il ou elle participera aussi au chapter web (regroupement de tous les développeurs full stack de l’entreprise).
 

Les à-côtés du poste 👁️
Le ou la stagiaire participera comme tous les ingénieurs à son chapter (réuni 2 fois par mois) dont le but est de :
  • Partager des connaissances entre ses membres (amélioration continue, bonnes pratiques)
  • Proposer des améliorations (nouveaux outils et processus)
  • Aider ses membres en fonction de leurs besoins

    • Ce qui t'attend si tu rejoins Doctrine 🤝

    • Contribuer à un projet ambitieux, avec un impact réel et positif sur la société : rendre le droit plus accessible et plus ouvert.
    • Un onboarding très complet permettant une intégration et une montée en compétence rapides.
    • Une aventure dans laquelle la formation et le partage des connaissances font partis du quotidien.
    • Rejoindre une entreprise avec une vie d’équipe riche et dynamique : conférences, team-buildings, déjeuner, offsite, afterwork, etc.

    Nos valeurs 🤝

    Chez Doctrine, nos 4 valeurs nous accompagnent au quotidien et dans notre ambition de faire bouger les choses.

    • Challenge the status quo : nous défendons les idées audacieuses qui contribuent à l’évolution de tout un secteur.
    • Liberty and responsibility : nous encourageons l’autonomie, l’impact de chacun·e et l’ownership.
    • Knowledge is power : l'information est au cœur de la mission de Doctrine, et nous cherchons constamment à progresser.
    • Release early, release often and listen to your customers : nous croyons au pouvoir de l’itération et à l’importance d’écouter en permanence notre marché, nos client·e·s et leurs problématiques.
     

    Nos avantages pour faire la différence ☀️

    🏡 Une politique de télétravail flexible permettant - selon les équipes - jusqu’à trois jours de télétravail par semaine.

    🌴 Une politique de congés flexibles

    🌱 Des opportunités concrètes de mobilité interne

    🏄‍♂️ Des évènements collectifs réguliers

    📚 Un vrai accent sur la formation individuelle et collective, avec un budget annuel de 750€ pour toute formation en lien avec ton poste - et des formations en équipe ou pour toute l'entreprise

    🏋️‍♀️ Un abonnement Gymlib pour les activités sportives et bien-être

    🧘 Un accès gratuit à la plateforme d'accompagnement à la santé mentale Moka.care et un accompagnement individuel allant jusqu’à 6 séances par an

    👩‍⚕️ Une assurance santé avec Alan

    🍱 🚲 Une carte Swile pour tes tickets restaurants et ton forfait mobilité durable (66,60 euros par mois)

    💡 Des réductions et avantages négociés grâce à notre CSE via la plateforme Happypal

    🍏 Un équipement de travail neuf chez Apple

     

    Notre processus de recrutement 🚀

    • Un premier échange de 30 min avec l’un.e de nos Talent Acquisition Manager pour bien comprendre ton projet professionnel et te présenter ce qu'on construit chez Doctrine
    • Une rencontre d’1h avec ton/ta futur.e manager, pour détailler le poste et le scope de l’équipe, mais aussi répondre à toutes tes questions.
    • Un ou deux tests techniques pour évaluer concrètement tes compétences
    • Une venue dans nos bureaux pour : un déjeuner avec 3 personnes de différents départements chez Doctrine, pour te donner un aperçu de tes futur.e.s collègues ; un échange sur les valeurs de l’entreprise pour te partager notre vision, et une rencontre avec notre CEO, Guillaume.
    (si nécessaire le processus pourra être adapté pour répondre à tes contraintes personnelles et professionnelles)
     
     
    Mesdames, autorisez-vous à candidater !
    Certaines études scientifiques montrent qu'en particulier les femmes ont moins tendance à postuler à une offre d'emploi quand elles n'ont pas toutes les qualifications. Si cela peut vous rassurer, sachez que cette fiche de poste est indicative donc prenez la comme telle : c'est un guide, ni plus ni moins.
    Si Doctrine vous intéresse, sachez que nous aurons plaisir à recevoir votre candidature !
     
    Diversité & inclusion
    Toutes nos offres sont ouvertes aux personnes en situation de handicap, n'hésitez pas a nous en parler lors du process de recrutement.
    Nous nous engageons à mettre en place tous les aménagements nécessaires pour garantir un environnement de travail adapté a chacun et chacune

Chargé·e de mission IA - AI Academy & adoption

About Scality

Scality solves organisations' biggest data storage challenges: growth, security, performance, and cost. Designed for end-to-end cyber resilience, only Scality S3 object storage with CORE5 safeguards data at every level of the system, from API to architecture. Its patented MultiScale Architecture enables limitless, independent scalability in all critical dimensions to meet the unpredictable demands of modern workloads. The world's most discerning companies depend on Scality to accelerate high-performance AI initiatives, optimize cloud deployments, and defend their data with confidence. Recognized as a leader by Gartner, Scality software is reliable, secure, and sustainable.


The mission

Teams across Scality, not only engineers, now build their own AI tools: skills, agents, connectors, websites. We want that to be fast, safe and shared, so nobody solves the same problem twice. You will run the program that makes it happen. That means the AI Academy, which teaches people to build with AI on their own work, and the standards that keep what they build safe and reusable.


What you will do
  • Run the AI Academy: cohorts, hands-on missions.
  • Get new builders set up in a day: accounts, access, their first tool.
  • Help teams describe their needs and find what already exists before anyone builds.
  • Keep the inventory of our AI tools current, and follow up on gaps with their owners.
  • Build skills and tools yourself with Claude Code, from your first weeks.
  • Prepare and follow up decisions with engineering, Security and leadership.
  • Keep people engaged: builder sessions, showcases, updates.

    • Who we are looking for
  • A recent graduate of a French grande école, or a student in your final year. Business school or a business–engineering double degree.
  • Little experience is fine. We hire for mindset, not for a CV.
  • You ask who has the problem before proposing a fix.
  • You check your work, and you never pass on AI output you have not checked.
  • You ship something rough quickly, then improve it.
  • You write short and plain, in French and English.
  • You are at ease with senior people, and persistent without being pushy.
  • You have built or run something on your own initiative: a side project, an association, a tool made with AI.

    • No coding is needed to apply. You will learn to build with AI here, and fast.


    What you get
  • Pay: €45,000–48,000 gross a year, fixed, for the CDI. €1,700 gross a month for the internship.
  • An office on Place de la Madeleine, in the heart of Paris. You work there 4 days a week, next to the people you help.
  • You learn to build with AI for real, with Claude Code, agents and MCP, instead of writing slides about it.
  • Company-wide scope from day one. You work directly with the person setting Scality's AI standards, and with engineering, Security and leadership.
  • Your work is used, and seen, across the company.
  • An international team across Europe, America, and Asia.
  • Training and professional certification programs, sports and wellness programs, social responsibility initiatives, and stock options distribution for CDI hires.

    • How to apply

    Apply on Lever with your CV and a 150-word answer to one question: explain something technical you learned recently to a colleague who is not technical.

    The process has four steps: your application, a 30-minute call, a two-hour exercise with Claude, a video interview with the CTO, and a final interview with 2 people at our Paris office.

    At Scality, we believe diversity drives innovation. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, welcoming applicants of all backgrounds, identities, and abilities. We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans.

Senior Automation & OT Engineer e/v/e/r/y/o/n/e
About Us

ten23 health is a human-centric and sustainable strategic partner of choice for the pharmaceutical industry and biotech start-ups for the development, manufacture, and testing of tomorrow’s medicines. We support our clients in developing differentiated, stable, usable, and safe injectable treatments for patients.


Your mission

We are looking for a Senior Automation & OT Engineer to develop our automation strategy while ensuring the day-to-day reliability, compliance, and continuous improvement of the operational technology running our production equipment. Sitting at the intersection of automation engineering and IT operations, you will lead complex projects and act as the primary technical expert for the shop floor. You will balance hands-on troubleshooting of PLCs and servers with structured, GMP-compliant change management to support safe, efficient manufacturing.

Key Responsibilities

  • Strategy & Leadership: Co - develop and support the site's overall automation strategy. Manage project pipelines, budgets, CAPEX/OPEX engineering tasks, and end-to-end hardware/software lifecycle planning.
  • Systems Operations & IT: Execute daily maintenance and troubleshooting for automation hardware (HMIs, PLCs). Administer if applicable underlying IT infrastructure, including Windows Servers, OS patching, OT network segmentation, and cybersecurity hygiene.
  • Process Equipment Expertise: Oversee automation systems for critical fill and finish operations, including filling lines, isolators, freeze dryers, autoclaves and building utilities.

jobs.title: Senior Embedded Linux Engineer
jobs.description:
Senior Embedded Linux Engineer

Gravis Robotics is a high-growth Series A start-up backed by SoftBank, bringing Physical AI to the construction industry, turning heavy construction machines into autonomous robots. 

Gravis began as an ETH Zurich spin-out, and our unique combination of learning-based automation and augmented remote control lets one operator safely conduct a fleet of earthmoving machines in a gamified environment. 

Backed by deep robotics research and now deployed across multiple countries with leading construction and equipment partners, our team is rapidly growing to bring this technology to a trillion-dollar industry. 

The Gravis RACK is a machine-agnostic retrofit kit that adds autonomy to excavators and wheel loaders from 10 to 100+ tonnes: LiDAR and camera sensing, GNSS RTK, networking hardware and rugged edge compute that works offline. Paired with the Slate tablet and our Copilot software, it lets an operator run a machine manually, with AI assistance, or fully autonomously.  Increasingly, we also build custom hardware to adapt our machines for highly specialized, robust applications beyond traditional excavation. 


About the role

At Gravis, we build high tech systems that give machine operators super human capabilities. To adapt in real time to changes in the environment the Gravis Rack fuses data from LiDAR, cameras, GNSS, and hydraulics into an autonomous control system. All of it runs on Linux, on compute hardware we design ourselves, bolted to the roof of a machine that vibrates, overheats, and regularly loses network coverage.

As a senior engineer focused on the embedded platform, you will own the software layer closest to that hardware: bootloader, kernel, device tree, root filesystem, and the update mechanism that keeps the fleet current. You will work at the intersection of our Hardware, Firmware, Autonomy, and Perception teams to bring up new boards alongside the engineers who designed them, then hand the software organization a platform they can build on without thinking about it. When something fails on site and nobody can yet say whether it's a driver or a solder joint, you are the person who finds out.


What you’ll do

  • Own the embedded Linux platform from end to end: bootloader, kernel, device tree and rootfs.

  • Bring up new hardware alongside electrical engineers.  Take our boards from first power-up to a boot you’d trust on a customer site.

  • Write and maintain the kernel drivers that connect the Rack’s sensors to the autonomy stack

  • Be the low level link between hardware and software teams; the person who can tell a driver bug from a hardware fault.

  • Drive our OTA update and recovery strategy for machines around the world

  • Implement security hardening: secure boot, disk encryption, container isolation, vulnerability patching.


    • What we're looking for

    We recognize that excellent candidates come from diverse backgrounds with varied combinations of skills. If you meet most of the core qualifications below, we encourage you to apply.

  • Degree in Electrical/Computer Engineering, CS, or related field.

  • Deep knowledge of Linux kernel internals: device drivers, device tree, interrupt handling, memory management, scheduling.

  • Experience with custom hardware bring-up: pin muxing, clock configuration, regulator control, PCIe, USB, I2C, SPI, UART, CSI, Ethernet.

  • Strong understanding of circuit diagrams and digital electronics.

  • Self-driven, able to take full ownership in a fast-moving startup.

  • Good English (written and spoken) is a must.


    • Bonus Qualifications

  • Yocto, Buildroot, nixOS or bootc experience for custom embedded distributions.

  • Experience with NVIDIA Jetson platforms (Thor, Orin, Xavier, Nano or equivalent) and JetPack/L4T ecosystem.

  • Power, thermal, or performance optimization on resource-constrained SoCs.

  • Familiar with CI/CD, Git, and automated build/deployment processes.

  • Know how to use debugging tools like JTAG, oscilloscopes, and logic analyzers.

  • Experience with the design, implementation and documentation of safety critical firmware

    •  

    This is an opportunity to join a dynamic, multidisciplinary team and to be part of a company that is reshaping heavy construction.

    Gravis is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse team, and do not discriminate based on race, colour, ancestry, national origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, gender identity, gender expression, disability, veteran status, or other legally protected characteristics.

Your focus will be on developing and optimizing model-serving architectures for advanced AI systems across a range of hardware environments.
You will tackle challenges involving latency, throughput, memory efficiency, and scalability, including deployment on resource-constrained mobile and edge devices.
The role combines hands-on research with low-level engineering, giving you the opportunity to develop novel inference strategies and GPU kernels.
You will work with complex architectures spanning text, image, audio, diffusion models, and vision transformers.

You will collaborate with cross-functional teams in a highly technical, remote environment focused on pushing the boundaries of efficient AI systems.

jobs.title: Regional Sales Manager (Mar y Sierras)
jobs.description:
Regional Sales Manager (Mar y Sierras)

About Halter

At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences. Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance. Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.

We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund, Bessemer Venture Partners, BOND, DCVC, Blackbird, Promus Ventures, Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures.

To find out more, visit our LinkedIn & Instagram.

About the role

This is a rare opportunity to be one of Halter's first Regional Sales Managers (Mar y Sierras) in Argentina — one of the world's great cattle nations — building our customer presence in the region from the ground up.

We're looking for a go-getter who is out in the field, meeting farmers, championing Halter and converting them into our very first local customers. A 'never give up attitude' is crucial for this role; as our first sales hire on the ground, you will be a foundational contributor to the growth and success of Halter in Argentina.

You'll be responsible for using your strong sales background to drive end-to-end sales, from cold calling and on-farm meetings to deeply understanding our customers' farm systems. You'll detail Halter's value proposition, progress the sale, and ultimately close the deal. As the region scales, you'll help shape how we set quotas and commissions, build sales capability, and mentor the team that follows you. Make your mark with Halter and help us push the boundaries of farming, connecting animals and humans like never before.

What your day could look like

  • Sourcing new leads and opportunities through proactive outreach, referrals/introductions, industry events and other channels, as well as fielding and responding to inbound inquiries.

  • Meeting high growth sales targets by managing pipeline through to close, including screening, qualifying, executing on-farm demonstrations and successfully negotiating contracts with customers.

  • Laying the groundwork for the local sales function — helping to set and manage quotas, commissions and other sales management tasks as the team grows.

  • Coaching, mentoring and developing future sales staff to help drive their professional growth and reach targets as we scale the region.

  • Collaborating with Customer Success to ensure successful post-sales handoff, implementations, customer satisfaction and account renewal.

  • Providing support, insight and communication to help build and foster trusting and enduring relationships with customers as they wait for deployment.

  • Leveraging opportunities and participating in relevant industry/Halter events and demonstrations.

  • Building and leveraging industry relationships to establish and maintain Halter's brand in a brand-new market.

  • Focusing on the customer and their needs, providing feedback to help drive the product roadmap.

  • Working with the team to optimise and evolve the sales process to become faster, more efficient and more predictable as the company scales.

Who are we looking for

  • A complete end-to-end sales skill set with at least five years of experience.

  • Proven track records and examples of successfully sourcing new prospects, securing meetings with new leads and creating new sales opportunities.

  • Someone highly experienced in value-based sales with a proven history of closing deals and high-volume sales results.

  • Well-prepared with solid communication skills to present Halter's value proposition.

  • Experience in beef farming or within the agricultural sector is highly desirable.

  • A person who is results-driven, highly motivated with exceptional time management skills.

  • Adaptability in a high-stakes sales environment and the ability to think on your feet — comfort with the ambiguity of building in a new market is a big plus.

  • Sales experience in the technology-based industry is preferred.

  • Fluency in Spanish, with professional working English to collaborate across our global team.

  • A university degree or equivalent would be excellent but not a must.

Halter in Argentina

Argentina is one of the largest beef producers and exporters in the world, with a deep grazing tradition across the Pampas and beyond. This is a founding role as Halter establishes itself in the region — meaning enormous scope to shape how an entire industry adopts virtual fencing technology. You'll be building from the ground up: our first customers, our first relationships, and the foundation of our local team. These opportunities don't come around often.

Join our team

Halter is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive workplace — a place where we can each be ourselves and do the best work of our lives. Research shows that while men apply to jobs when they meet an average of 60% of the requirements, women and under-represented groups of candidates tend to only apply when they meet every requirement. If you think you have what it takes but don’t necessarily tick every requirement on this job description, please still get in touch and apply to Halter. We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit!

If this opportunity sounds like you, please apply below by sending through your cover letter explaining why you’re excited about this role and working at Halter, along with your CV, and we’ll be in touch!

Please also feel free to check out the careers page for more information on working at Halter and don't forget to follow us on LinkedIn & Instagram.

Why our team loves working at Halter:

  • Work that genuinely matters. Every now and again a company comes along that transforms an entire industry and leaves the world in a better place. Our team gets to be part of something truly meaningful, helping farmers improve their livelihoods, spend more time with their families, and build more sustainable operations.

  • Spectacular people solving hard problems. Our culture is designed for talented people to do work that changes lives. The team is filled with diverse, kind, and driven people who push each other to do their best work. You'll be thrown into the deep end, tackling complex challenges and building something tangible that solves real problems.

  • You'll grow here. Autonomy, mastery, and learning define how we work. You'll have the freedom to work on interesting problems, master new skills, and continuously develop yourself, both through your role and our $1,000 personal growth fund.

  • This isn't easy, and we love that it's hard. Working at Halter will be the most rewarding and the most challenging work of your life. We move fast, take bold bets, and work hard to reshape an entire industry. As one team member put it: "Joining Halter is a bit like strapping yourself to a rocket ship, but it's an epic journey to be a part of!"

Full-Time Argentina
